name: Rakiura Track
why: An island circuit at an easy pace: beaches on the open coast to Port William, then old sawmill tramlines through podocarp forest to the quiet shores of Paterson Inlet, with kiwi calling at night.
book: All huts and campsites must be booked, all year. Reach Oban by a 1 hour ferry from Bluff or a 20 minute flight from Invercargill. From Oban it is 5 km by road to Lee Bay (shuttles run) and 2 km back from Fern Gully car park.
water: Each campsite has a water supply; treat or boil water before drinking.
dangers: Between Port William and North Arm, mud can rise above boot height for up to 500 m after rain: wear gaiters.
Strong wind, hail and heavy rain can come at any time of year.
The creeks at Little River and Māori Beach can be waded only at low tide; at high tide use the track and bridges.
turnaround: After long rain, ask at the Rakiura National Park Visitor Centre in Oban before leaving Port William; if the inland section is too wet, walk back to Lee Bay.

points.name: Lee Bay chain sculpture
points.note: The track enters the national park through the giant anchor-chain sculpture at Lee Bay, 5 km from Oban.

points.name: Port William Hut
points.note: First night by Magnetic Beach in Port William / Potirepo, after Māori Beach and its old sawmill boiler.

points.name: North Arm Hut
points.note: Second night on Paterson Inlet, after 13 km of forest and log-hauler relics from the milling days.

points.name: Fern Gully car park
points.note: End of the track after Sawdust Bay and Kaipipi Bay on the old Kaipipi Road; Oban is 2 km down the road.
